Resolve GitHub issue https://github.com/softwaremill/sttp/issues/2963 ("Remove fs2 interop with reactive-streams").

Problem: `HttpClientFs2Backend` (effects/fs2/src/main/scalajvm/sttp/client4/httpclient/fs2/HttpClientFs2Backend.scala) converts between java.util.concurrent.Flow and fs2 streams via `org.reactivestreams.FlowAdapters` + `fs2.interop.reactivestreams` (`toStreamBuffered`, `StreamUnicastPublisher`). That interop doesn't support cancellation (https://github.com/typelevel/fs2/issues/3260): when a streaming response body (e.g. SSE) is interrupted, e.g. with `timeoutOnPullTo`, cancellation never completes, the connection stays open and the app can't shut down. The reporter confirmed that using fs2's native Flow interop (`fs2.interop.flow`, e.g. `fs2.Stream.fromPublisher`) fixes it.

Goal:
- In effects/fs2 (fs2 3.x, cats-effect 3) `HttpClientFs2Backend`, replace the reactive-streams interop with `fs2.interop.flow` for both directions: response body (Flow.Publisher -> fs2 Stream) and streaming request body (fs2 Stream -> Flow.Publisher for `BodyPublishers.fromPublisher`). Drop the `FlowAdapters` / `fs2.interop.reactivestreams` usage there, and remove the now-unused reactive-streams related dependencies of that module from build.sbt if nothing else in the module needs them.
- Do NOT change effects/fs2-ce2 (fs2 2.x has no Flow interop) nor the Armeria backends (Armeria's API is reactive-streams based).
- Keep behaviour otherwise identical (buffering, chunking, error handling).
- Add a test (in the fs2 module's existing test suite for the HttpClient fs2 backend) showing that interrupting a streamed response body (e.g. take a few elements of an infinite/long SSE or streaming endpoint from the test server, or apply a timeout) completes and does not hang. Use existing test-server endpoints if possible.
- Existing fs2 HttpClient backend tests must pass.

Build caveat: sbt does NOT load inside this git worktree (JGit NoWorkTreeException from a git plugin). To compile/test: `git clone --shared /home/adamw/sttp <scratch>/build`, check out the same commit as HEAD here, apply this worktree's diff (`git add -N . && git diff HEAD | (cd <scratch>/build && git apply)`), and run sbt there, e.g. `sbt "testScoped 3 JVM"` scoped to the fs2 module (find the project id via `sbt projects`; join multiple sbt commands with `;` in one argument). Copy any scalafmt changes back. If recompiles fail with AccessDeniedException, delete the affected module's `target/out` dir.

resultJson.description:
Resolve softwaremill/sttp#2963: `HttpClientFs2Backend` (fs2 3.x / cats-effect 3, module `effects/fs2`) currently bridges java.net.http's `java.util.concurrent.Flow` publishers to fs2 streams through `org.reactivestreams.FlowAdapters` and `fs2.interop.reactivestreams` (`toStreamBuffered`, `StreamUnicastPublisher`). That reactive-streams interop does not support cancellation (typelevel/fs2#3260): when a streamed response body (e.g. SSE) is interrupted with `take`, `timeoutOnPullTo`, etc., the cancellation never completes, the connection stays open and the application cannot shut down.

The epic switches both directions of the bridge to fs2's native Flow interop (`Stream.fromPublisher` for response bodies, `Stream#subscribe` backed by the backend's existing `Dispatcher` for request bodies), keeping chunking/buffering/error behaviour identical, and then drops the `fs2-reactive-streams` dependency from the `fs2` module's JVM settings in build.sbt since nothing else in the module uses it. A regression test in the HttpClient fs2 streaming suite shows that interrupting a streamed response body completes promptly. `effects/fs2-ce2` (fs2 2.x has no Flow interop) and the Armeria backends (reactive-streams based API) stay untouched.

tasks.title: Response body: use fs2 Flow interop (Stream.fromPublisher) and add interruption regression test
tasks.description:
In `effects/fs2/src/main/scalajvm/sttp/client4/httpclient/fs2/HttpClientFs2Backend.scala`, replace `lowLevelBodyToBody`:

```scala
FlowAdapters.toPublisher(p).toStreamBuffered[F](1).flatMap(...)
```
with `fs2.Stream.fromPublisher[F](p, chunkSize = 1)` (the `FromPublisherPartiallyApplied` overload taking a `java.util.concurrent.Flow.Publisher[ju.List[ByteBuffer]]`), keeping the same `flatMap(data => Stream.emits(data.asScala.map(Chunk.byteBuffer)).flatMap(Stream.chunk))` conversion. chunkSize 1 preserves the previous request-one-at-a-time buffering. Remove the now unused `fs2.interop.reactivestreams.PublisherOps` import (leave the request-side imports for the next task).

Add a test to `effects/fs2/src/test/scalajvm/sttp/client4/httpclient/fs2/HttpClientFs2StreamingTest.scala` (currently an empty class body; add an `in` block there, not in the shared `Fs2StreamingTest`): send `basicRequest.get(uri"$endpoint/streaming/slow").response(asStreamAlwaysUnsafe(streams))` (declare the request with an explicit `StreamRequest[Stream[IO, Byte], Fs2Streams[IO]]` type as other unsafe tests do, for Scala 3), then `response.body.take(1).compile.drain` wrapped in `.timeout(10.seconds)` so a hang becomes a failure, measure elapsed time with `IO.monotonic` and assert it is below 2 seconds (the endpoint streams 20 chunks over 2s). Convert to Future with `.toFuture()` / `convertToFuture`. Add a short comment explaining the endpoint timing and that this guards against the cancellation hang from issue #2963.

Follow TDD: build in the scratch clone and run the test against the old implementation first to confirm it fails (hangs → TimeoutException). If `take(1)` does not reproduce the hang, use the reporter's scenario instead: `uri"$endpoint/sse/echo3"` (POST with a body, emits 3 events 500ms apart) with `.timeoutOnPullTo(200.millis, Stream.empty)` or `.interruptAfter`. Then apply the change and run the whole fs2 JVM HttpClient test suite (`HttpClientFs2StreamingTest`, `HttpClientFs2HttpTest`, `HttpClientFs2WebSocketTest`) on Scala 3; all must pass.

tasks.title: Request body: build the Flow.Publisher with Stream#subscribe and remove the reactive-streams dependency
tasks.description:
In `HttpClientFs2Backend.streamToPublisher` replace

```scala
BodyPublishers.fromPublisher(FlowAdapters.toFlowPublisher(StreamUnicastPublisher(stream.chunks.map(_.toByteBuffer), dispatcher): org.reactivestreams.Publisher[ByteBuffer]))
```
with a `java.util.concurrent.Flow.Publisher[ByteBuffer]` built from fs2's Flow interop. `Stream#toPublisherResource` needs a Resource scope we don't have here and `unsafeToPublisher` is IO-only, so mirror fs2's own `DispatcherStreamPublisher`: an anonymous `Flow.Publisher[ByteBuffer]` whose `subscribe(subscriber)` runs `dispatcher.unsafeRunAndForget(byteBuffers.subscribe(subscriber).compile.drain)` where `byteBuffers = stream.chunks.map(_.toByteBuffer)` (cast the `Subscriber[_ >: ByteBuffer]` to `Subscriber[ByteBuffer]` if inference needs it). `Stream#subscribe` performs `onSubscribe`, honours backpressure and shuts down gracefully on `cancel()`. Keep it wrapped in `monad.eval(BodyPublishers.fromPublisher(...))`. Add a brief comment on why the publisher is hand-rolled (no Resource scope; reuse the backend's dispatcher). Put the small publisher in a private helper (method or a `private[fs2]` class in the same package) rather than inline, with a usage-focused doc comment.

Remove the remaining `fs2.interop.reactivestreams.StreamUnicastPublisher` and `org.reactivestreams.FlowAdapters` imports. Then in `build.sbt`, in `lazy val fs2` → `.jvmPlatform(... libraryDependencies ++= Seq(...))` (around line 492), delete the `"co.fs2" %% "fs2-reactive-streams" % fs2_3_version` line, leaving `fs2-io`. Do NOT touch `fs2Ce2` (line ~470) or the `armeriaFs2Backend` / `armeriaFs2Ce2Backend` entries (lines ~764/773), which declare their own `fs2-reactive-streams` dependency. Grep `effects/fs2` to confirm no other `org.reactivestreams` / `fs2.interop.reactivestreams` usages remain.

Verify in the scratch clone: compile the fs2 module for Scala 2.12, 2.13 and 3 on JVM (`compileScoped` or the per-project ids), and run the fs2 JVM HttpClient test suite on Scala 3; the existing request-streaming tests ("stream request body", "stream large request body", "stream request body with known length", "send a stream part in a multipart request") cover this path. Also compile `armeriaFs2Backend` to make sure it still resolves `fs2.interop.reactivestreams` from its own dependency. Copy any scalafmt reformatting back to the worktree.

resultJson.brief:
## Modules and files

- `effects/fs2/` — fs2 3.x + cats-effect 3 integration (sbt project matrix `fs2`, JVM/JS/Native, Scala 2.12/2.13/3). Only the JVM source dir matters here.
  - `effects/fs2/src/main/scalajvm/sttp/client4/httpclient/fs2/HttpClientFs2Backend.scala` — the backend to change. Extends `HttpClientAsyncBackend[F, Fs2Streams[F], Publisher[ju.List[ByteBuffer]], Stream[F, Byte]]` (Publisher = `java.util.concurrent.Flow.Publisher`). Holds a `dispatcher: Dispatcher[F]` (also used by `Fs2SimpleQueue`). Two methods bridge Flow ⇄ fs2:
    - `override protected def lowLevelBodyToBody(p: Publisher[util.List[ByteBuffer]]): Stream[F, Byte]` — response side; currently `FlowAdapters.toPublisher(p).toStreamBuffered[F](1).flatMap(data => Stream.emits(data.asScala.map(Chunk.byteBuffer)).flatMap(Stream.chunk))`.
    - `override def streamToPublisher(stream: Stream[F, Byte]): F[HttpRequest.BodyPublisher]` inside the anonymous `BodyToHttpClient` — request side; currently `monad.eval(BodyPublishers.fromPublisher(FlowAdapters.toFlowPublisher(StreamUnicastPublisher(stream.chunks.map(_.toByteBuffer), dispatcher))))`. Also used by the multipart builder via `toPublisher`.
    - `cancelLowLevelBody` delegates to `sttp.client4.internal.httpclient.cancelPublisher` (core, Flow-based) — unchanged.
    - Imports to drop when done: `fs2.interop.reactivestreams.PublisherOps`, `fs2.interop.reactivestreams.StreamUnicastPublisher`, `org.reactivestreams.FlowAdapters`. These are the only reactive-streams usages in `effects/fs2` (grep confirmed).
  - `effects/fs2/src/main/scalajvm/sttp/client4/httpclient/fs2/Fs2BodyFromHttpClient.scala` — maps the `Stream[F, Byte]` to response-as types; `regularAsStream` returns `(stream, () => stream.compile.drain.handleError(...))`. No change needed; useful to understand that `asStreamAlways` drains after the user function and `asStreamAlwaysUnsafe` hands the raw stream to the caller.
  - Tests (JVM): `effects/fs2/src/test/scalajvm/sttp/client4/httpclient/fs2/HttpClientFs2StreamingTest.scala` is `class HttpClientFs2StreamingTest extends Fs2StreamingTest with HttpClientFs2TestBase` with an empty body — the place for the new test. `HttpClientFs2TestBase` provides `implicit val backend: WebSocketStreamBackend[IO, Fs2Streams[IO]] = HttpClientFs2Backend[IO](dispatcher).unsafeRunSync()`, `dispatcher` from `TestIODispatcher`, and via `CatsTestBase`: `implicit ioRuntime`, `implicit convertToFuture: ConvertToFuture[IO]`, `timeoutToNone[T](t: IO[T], timeoutMillis: Int): IO[Option[T]]`. `Fs2StreamingTest` (`effects/fs2/src/test/scala/.../impl/fs2/Fs2StreamingTest.scala`) is shared with JS, so don't put HttpClient-specific tests there. It defines `streams: Fs2Streams[IO]`, `bodyConsumer`, `sseConsumer`.
  - Generic streaming suite: `core/src/test/scala/sttp/client4/testing/streaming/StreamingTest.scala` (AsyncFreeSpec, `ToFutureWrapper` gives `.toFuture()` on `F[_]`). Unsafe-stream tests there declare requests with explicit types, e.g. `val r0: StreamRequest[streams.BinaryStream, S] = basicRequest.post(...).response(asStreamAlwaysUnsafe(streams))` because of Scala 3 inference. `endpoint` comes from `sttp.client4.testing.HttpTest.endpoint`.
- Test server (`testing/server/.../HttpServer.scala`, akka-http, started automatically by `testServerSettings`): `GET /streaming/slow` — chunked response, 20 chunks of "a", one per 100ms (2s total). `POST /sse/echo3` — emits 3 SSE events with the request body as data, every 500ms, then completes. `HttpTest` already uses `/streaming/slow` with a `< 2000L` elapsed assertion (line ~797) — a pattern to copy.
- `build.sbt`: `val fs2_3_version = "3.14.0"`, `val fs2_2_version = "2.5.13"`. `lazy val fs2` (line ~477) adds `"co.fs2" %% "fs2-reactive-streams" % fs2_3_version` and `"co.fs2" %% "fs2-io"` in `.jvmPlatform(...)` settings (line ~492). `fs2Ce2` (line ~470), `armeriaFs2Backend` (line ~773) and `armeriaFs2Ce2Backend` (line ~764) declare their own `fs2-reactive-streams` — leave them. `docs/` has no mention of fs2-reactive-streams.
- Do not touch `effects/fs2-ce2/.../HttpClientFs2Backend.scala` or `armeria-backend/fs2*`.

## fs2 3.14 Flow interop API (java.util.concurrent.Flow, in fs2-core, no extra dependency)

- `Stream.fromPublisher[F]: FromPublisherPartiallyApplied[F]`, then `.apply[A](publisher: Flow.Publisher[A], chunkSize: Int)(implicit F: Async[F]): Stream[F, A]`. chunkSize = number of elements requested at a time; the stream emits only when a chunk fills or the publisher completes, so use `1` to match the old `toStreamBuffered(1)`. Subscribes lazily when the stream runs; cancellation of the stream cancels the Flow subscription.
- `Stream#subscribe[F2[x] >: F[x]: Async, O2 >: O](subscriber: Flow.Subscriber[O2]): Stream[F2, Nothing]` — calls `onSubscribe`, feeds the subscriber with backpressure, runs until consumed; cancelling the stream (or the subscriber calling `cancel()`) shuts down gracefully.
- `Stream#toPublisherResource[F2, O2]: Resource[F2, Flow.Publisher[O2]]` (allocates its own `Dispatcher.parallel`) and `Stream[IO, A].unsafeToPublisher()(implicit IORuntime)` — not usable here (no Resource scope in `streamToPublisher`, and F is generic). fs2's internal `StreamPublisher`/`StreamSubscription` are `private[fs2]`; its `DispatcherStreamPublisher.subscribe` is just `requireNonNull(subscriber)`, build subscription, `dispatcher.unsafeRunAndForget(subscription.run.compile.drain)` — reproduce that with the public `Stream#subscribe` and the backend's existing `dispatcher`.
- `fs2.interop.flow` package-object functions exist but are deprecated in favour of the `Stream` methods above; use the `Stream` methods.

## Conventions

- Scala 2.12/2.13/3 cross-build: avoid Scala-3-only syntax in main sources except what's already there (`using` appears in `HttpClientFs2Backend` companion only in Scala-3-compatible positions; the file compiles on 2.12 too, so keep to `implicitly`/standard syntax). `scala.collection.JavaConverters._` is used for `asScala`.
- Comments: only explain non-obvious reasoning; no restating code. Doc comments on new helpers describe usage/invariants, not implementation.
- Tests are ScalaTest AsyncFreeSpec `"..." in { ... }` returning `Future[Assertion]`; convert IO via `.toFuture()` (ToFutureWrapper + implicit ConvertToFuture[IO]).
- Never commit. Keep scalafmt formatting (run `scalafmtAll` or copy formatter changes back from the scratch clone).

## Build / test (sbt does NOT load in this worktree)

`git clone --shared /home/adamw/sttp <scratch>/build`, check out the same commit as HEAD here, then `git add -N . && git diff HEAD | (cd <scratch>/build && git apply)`; run sbt in the clone. Join multiple sbt commands with `;` inside one argument (`sbt -batch "a" "b"` only runs the first). Project ids follow sbt-projectmatrix naming (JVM has no platform suffix, Scala suffix `3` / `2_13` / `2_12`, e.g. `fs23`, `fs22_13`; confirm with `sbt projects`). Scoped helpers: `sbt "compileScoped 3 JVM"`, `sbt "testScoped 3 JVM"` (whole build — slow; prefer `fs23/testOnly sttp.client4.httpclient.fs2.*`). Tests need the test server, started automatically by `testServerSettings`. If recompiles fail with `AccessDeniedException` on CAS symlinks, delete the affected module's `target/out/...` dir and rebuild.

resultJson.title: Use fs2 Flow interop instead of reactive-streams in HttpClientFs2Backend
resultJson.body:
`HttpClientFs2Backend` (fs2 3.x) converted between `java.util.concurrent.Flow` and fs2 streams using `FlowAdapters` and `fs2.interop.reactivestreams`. That interop doesn't support cancellation (typelevel/fs2#3260). For example, interrupting a streamed response body (such as SSE) with `timeoutOnPullTo` never finished, the connection stayed open, and the app couldn't shut down.

- Response body: now uses `Stream.fromPublisher` with `chunkSize = 1`, matching the old `toStreamBuffered(1)` buffering.
- Request body: now uses a small `Flow.Publisher` that runs `Stream#subscribe` on the backend's `Dispatcher`. `toPublisherResource` can't be used here because it needs a `Resource` scope, which isn't available when the request body is created.
- Removed the `fs2-reactive-streams` dependency from the `fs2` module. `fs2-ce2` and the Armeria backends are unchanged and keep their own dependency.
- Tests: added a `/streaming/stall` test-server endpoint, which sends one chunk and then keeps the connection open. New tests check that cancelling a response stream while it waits for data completes, and that cancelling a request while its body is streaming finalizes that body stream. Another new test checks that a failing request body stream fails the request.

Closes #2963
